item.title: brutal fantasies is literally the peak of human existence
item.description: ok.. i'm coming back from the dead again to talk about the only album that matters right now, and i know its late talking about it. sorry not sorry.
item.content:encoded:
why im back (again)

it has been almost a week since i last posted but i literally dont care because i took like a month long break before that so i have energy again. the urge called and i answered with a blog post :)

i was gonna talk about sukkubys or blade and bath coming back to life because that whole scene is actually moving lately but i had a realization...

the only thing that matters

brutal fantasies is literally the best album on this planet. no contest. its peak. its the absolute ceiling of the genre.

everyone else can stop recording now because this is it. the atmosphere is perfect. the production? exactly what it needs to be. the absolute dread and instrumental?? oh my god! this is modern beethoven! i have been looping this and nothing else is hitting the same right now. WHAT ARE THEY FEEDING THESE ARTISTS?!

this is kinda what i noticed on the album..

  • vocals that actually hurt to listen to (in a REALLY good way)
  • that specific raw energy that most dsbm bands try to fake but totally fail at
  • literally no skips!
albumrating
Brutal Fantasies11/10
Soundtrack for a Suicide: Opus II11/10
Eternal Damnation11/10
..Of Mourning10/10
and everything elseMID!

anyways, happy wallowing!

item.title: ricing supremacy and why ricing makes you an actually better dev
item.description: PLEASE stop staring at ugly default themes. your environment is a reflection of your work.
item.content:encoded:
aesthetic is actual efficiency (dont @ me!)

if you're still on any default terminal theme, i'm praying for you. making things look good isn't just a "ricer on reddit" thing but more about building a comfortable space where you actually want to suffer through merge conflicts!

why color palettes?

it's the total peak of human engineering. colors, decent contrast, and something that won't torch your retinas at midnight

final thoughts

stop settling for defaults. start spending time actually configuring your colorscheme instead of shipping :). it's actually something called investment.

"also, if your terminal is ugly, your logic is probably ugly too :3" - virex ong

item.title: turning ewaste into a small dev rig
item.description: this is why I decided to torture myself by putting debian on a snappy chromebook and how it actually kinda works!
item.content:encoded:
why do i do this to myself?

there is something so satisfying about taking a "dead" chromebook and making it run a real OS. my old hp x360 (aka snappy) was basically a paperweight, but now it's a dedicated debian 13 box.

the setup

  • OS: debian 13. because I like living on the edge of "stable"
  • DE: GNOME classic. it's heavy for these specs but it just feels like home.
  • editor: vim. the only editor that belongs on a screen this bad.

"it's not ewaste if you can still run a terminal on it."

item.title: sysdupd: arch updates without the headache
item.description: i finally got tired of manual pacman runs, so i built a libadwaita manager for personal use.
item.content:encoded:
it finally works. built a custom update manager using Python, GTK4, and libadwaita.

  • systemd timers for background checks
  • dynamic distro detection
  • background service integration
  • sleek adwaita interface

check the source on my GitHub (hnpf) or install via aur: yay -S sysdupd

item.title: long term pixel 10 pro use: my review of the tensor G5
item.description: the 3nm transition, on-device AI, and why the pixel 10 pro is finally a consistent daily driver.
item.content:encoded:
the TSMC shift

moving to TSMC's 3nm process makes efficiency gains immediately apparent. thermals stay stable under sustained loads, and the nona-core CPU config with cortex-x4 at 3.78GHz got a real lift in single-thread perf.

memory and multitasking

16GB LPDDR5X handles aggressive background processes without the usual cached app culling.

camera and computer vision

the new ISP allows 100x zoom using on-device generative models. video boost is now handled locally on the TPU instead of cloud-side.

platform stability

Android 16 builds are surprisingly solid. the level of control in the modern Android stack is peaking.

item.title: your cloud is just someone else's computer.
item.description: this is why i hoard data (and you probably should too)
item.content:encoded:
stop trusting corporations with your data.

  • if it's on my drive, no one can "un-license" it.
  • paying $15/month for a library that changes every week is a joke.
  • i keep games, movies, and tools because once they're gone from the web, they're gone forever.

it's about digital sovereignty. they don't care about your files, they care about your subscription.

item.title: why I actually use arch.. (and it's not a joke)
item.description: I just want a system that doesn't hand bs over to me...
item.content:encoded:
• no bloat: exactly what i need and nothing else.
  • the wiki: the holy grail of documentation.
  • rolling release: latest kernel features immediately.
  • my rig (RX 6800 XT / i5-14600K) runs much better when i own the hardware instead of the OS owning me.

item.title: the internet is dead.
item.description: if you think you're talking to real people on the big platforms anymore, i have a bridge to sell you.
item.content:encoded:
this is why i self host.

socials are just bots talking to bots.

  • AI-generated slop consumed by AI-generated scrapers.
  • "blue checks" with generic AI names replying to everything.
  • algorithms showing what keeps you scrolling, not what is good.

AI already killed the web. go outside.

item.title: the epstein "files" are a joke
item.description: the DOJ finally dropped the files and... surprise! it's basically 50 pages of blacked out text.
item.content:encoded:
the most transparent administration?

the DOJ documents are so redacted they look like modern art.

  • missed deadlines.
  • "rolling releases" that are just more redactions.
  • files disappearing after being posted.

it's embarrassing how much effort goes into hiding names despite the law.

item.title: why i love open source
item.description: honestly, open source is just built different.
item.content:encoded:
• peek under the hood of massive projects.
  • see how pros actually build things.
  • contributing > gatekeeping.
  • community feedback makes things 10x more secure.
